Back-office purchasing/reporting/settings may remain online-only.

tasks.title: Build public Shop slug, tenant URL and publication foundation
tasks.description: Create the public-website identity layer. Published Shops use https://{shop-slug}.shops.building-suit.com. Store slug separately from Shop name; propose it from the Shop name, enforce lowercase ASCII letters/numbers/hyphens, reserved-name rejection and case-insensitive uniqueness, support explicit slug changes with old-slug redirects, and fail closed on unknown/unpublished hosts. Prepare/document wildcard DNS/Vercel requirements but do not mutate provider configuration.
verification_plan: DB tests for slug normalization, reserved names, collisions, concurrent claims, aliases and non-reuse.
Host-resolution tests for valid, unknown, unpublished and cross-Shop requests.
Slug-change redirect tests; Shop typecheck/lint/tests/build and git diff --check.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical public URL is https://{slug}.shops.building-suit.com and the private owner/staff app remains a separate host.
Slug is stored independently from Shop display name; renaming the Shop never silently changes its URL.
Slug rules are deterministic, 3-50 chars, lowercase ASCII letters/numbers/hyphens, with reserved-name protection and concurrency-safe case-insensitive uniqueness.
For non-Latin/ambiguous names, generation uses a safe collision-resistant fallback and remains owner-editable before publish.
Explicit slug changes preserve old aliases that only redirect to the same Shop; old slugs are not immediately reusable by another Shop.
Unknown, suspended, archived or unpublished tenant hosts fail closed and do not leak another tenant.
Provider/DNS wildcard activation is documented as a separate release action and is not performed by this task.

tasks.title: Add public Shop profile, required logo, contacts, locations and publish readiness
tasks.description: Add Business settings for the public website. Publication is opt-in and requires a logo, public Shop name, short description, at least one public contact method, at least one explicitly visible active location, and at least one published product/service. Support public phone, WhatsApp and email plus public location presentation/opening-hours data and SEO fields without auto-publishing private operational data.
verification_plan: Owner/settings-manager happy path and unauthorized/cross-Shop denial.
Publication readiness matrix and publish/unpublish/republish tests.
acceptance_criteria: Business settings shows public-site draft/published state and canonical tenant URL.
Publish is blocked until logo, public name, description, one contact method, one visible active location and one published product/service are present.
Logo accepts bounded safe raster formats such as PNG/JPEG/WebP; arbitrary unsanitized SVG is rejected.
Logo/assets are tenant-scoped and cannot be read or replaced across Shops.
Phone, WhatsApp and email are independently configurable/public.
Active operational locations are not public by default; owner explicitly selects visible locations and public fields.
Unpublish removes public content immediately while preserving configuration for later republish.
Publication/profile writes are permission checked and audited.

tasks.title: Add selective public product and service publishing
tasks.description: Create an explicit public-catalog layer. Internal active products/services remain private until the owner publishes them. Support public description, optional image, display order and per-item Show price. Never expose cost, FIFO, internal stock, supplier/private fields, internal notes or unrelated IDs. No ecommerce behavior.
verification_plan: Shown/hidden price tests in EN/AR and cross-Shop authorization tests.
acceptance_criteria: Active products/services remain private until explicitly published.
Publish/unpublish never changes operational active/archive state.
Per item supports public description, optional image, display order and Show price toggle.
Hidden price produces a contact-for-price presentation and is absent from public payloads.
Archived/inactive items automatically disappear publicly while publication configuration may be preserved.
Public projection is allowlisted and excludes cost/FIFO/stock quantities/supplier-private/internal-note data.
Cross-Shop item references are rejected server-side.
No cart, checkout, order, reservation or payment behavior is introduced.

tasks.title: Build the bilingual public Shop showcase and contact experience
tasks.description: Build the customer-facing tenant website from public projections: Shop identity, selected services/products, visible locations, phone, WhatsApp, email and a bounded contact form. Store inquiries for the Shop owner. V1 is showcase/contact only: no booking, cart, checkout, payment, stock reservation, ordering or customer account creation.
acceptance_criteria: Published tenant URL renders only the resolved Shop public profile/catalog/locations.
Public website is responsive, accessible and bilingual EN/AR with correct RTL/LTR.
Phone, WhatsApp and email actions appear only when configured/public.
Contact form collects bounded name/contact/message and stores an inquiry for the resolved Shop.
Inquiry submission uses server validation, honeypot and rate limiting; anonymous users cannot read inquiry storage.
Owner can view/manage own website inquiries; no cross-Shop access.
Unknown/unpublished Shops do not render stale cached tenant content.
Canonical URL, meta description, Open Graph and robots behavior are correct; unpublished sites are noindex/fail closed.
No ecommerce or public booking controls exist.

tasks.title: Issue secure appointment access codes and short-lived customer portal sessions
tasks.description: Extend appointments with customer-facing access credentials. Issue cryptographically random non-sequential human-readable codes; authorized staff can issue/rotate them for existing appointments. Code plus matching normalized phone is required. Successful verification creates only a high-entropy short-lived Shop/customer-scoped session. Rate-limit and audit attempts without logging secrets.
verification_plan: Rate-limit/brute-force, rotate/revoke/session-expiry and cross-Shop replay tests.
acceptance_criteria: Codes are cryptographically random/non-sequential using a human-friendly alphabet with at least about 50 bits of entropy.
Code alone never returns appointment/customer history; matching normalized phone is required.
Mismatch responses avoid revealing whether code, phone, Shop or customer exists.
Successful verification creates a short-lived token scoped to exactly one Shop and one saved customer or one walk-in appointment.
Codes/sessions can be rotated/revoked and prior access stops working.
Full codes/session secrets never appear in ordinary logs/audit/error text.
Verification is rate-limited at appropriate client/Shop/credential boundaries.
Appointment edits do not silently rotate access credentials.
Appointment without usable phone cannot enable portal access until phone is safely captured or it is linked to a saved customer.
Existing scheduling, availability, idempotency and audit behavior remains intact.

tasks.title: Build the secure public customer appointment and service-history portal
tasks.description: Add My appointments to each public Shop website. A verified saved customer sees only same-Shop upcoming/past appointment and service history: date/time, public location, service, assigned staff display name and status. Walk-ins are appointment-scoped. Exclude financial records, internal notes and private staff/customer fields.
verification_plan: Saved-customer upcoming/past fixture and walk-in fixture.
Payload allowlist proving financial/private fields absent.
acceptance_criteria: Public website has a clear My appointments/history entry point.
No history is queryable without a valid short-lived portal session.
Saved customer sees only same-Shop upcoming/past appointments/services with date/time, public location, service, staff display name and status.
Appointment notes, staff contact details, sales, invoices, receipts, payments, balances, product purchase history and internal audit data are excluded.
Walk-in session exposes only its verified appointment and cannot broaden by matching name/phone.
Cancelled/no-show/completed statuses render accurately.
Expired/revoked session returns to verification without exposing cached prior history.
EN/AR mobile-first accessibility and RTL/LTR pass.

tasks.title: Canonical UI PRO methodology, evidence baseline and plan audit
tasks.description:
OBJECTIVE: Adopt the permanent Building Suit UI PRO methodology in canonical shared documentation and refresh the evidence baseline/task audit before any UI implementation.

USER / PROBLEM: Building Suit already has a capable shared design system, but future AI sessions need a durable evidence-led method that prevents generic AI-template composition and treats external products as UX behavior references, never branding authority.

CURRENT-STATE EVIDENCE: Inspect current AGENTS rules, shared design/UI ownership/interaction/table docs, canonical tokens, shell, Shop dashboard, Ledger dashboard, available Inventory UI, and the current BS-UI-PRO control-plane graph at the execution-time repository ref. Preserve correct behavior and record unverified areas.

REFERENCE-PATTERN EVIDENCE: Define the focused research record. Normally use one best-in-class general reference, one relevant domain reference, and optionally one strong alternate/open-source reference per UX question. Record observed pattern, why it works, applicability, adaptation, adopt/adapt/reject, affected scope and evidence limit.

BUILDING SUIT ADAPTATION: Materialize the approved methodology at docs/shared/ui-pro-task-guide.md and index it from docs/shared/README.md if current documentation convention requires it. Do not alter product UI, tokens, business logic, databases, n8n, deployment configuration or framework dependencies.
verification_plan: Read root/scoped AGENTS and canonical shared UI specifications.
Run relevant docs generation/checks plus git diff --check.
Review the final guide as a fresh-session handoff and confirm only allowed docs paths changed.
acceptance_criteria: docs/shared/ui-pro-task-guide.md exists as the canonical cross-Suit UI PRO methodology and is discoverable from shared docs.

The guide contains authority hierarchy, reverse-engineering methodology, research fields, page archetypes, component ownership, task-authoring, visual-acceptance, pilot-before-propagation and anti-pattern rules.
Current UI baseline is refreshed against the execution-time ref and distinguishes correct behavior from composition gaps.
Existing BS-UI-PRO-001..010 tasks are audited without discarding valid IDs and the pilot approval gate is recorded.
Future browser/rendered verification capability is confirmed or explicitly BLOCKED/NOT VERIFIED.
No application UI or domain behavior is changed.

tasks.title: Professionalize shared application shell and navigation
tasks.description:
OBJECTIVE: Make the authenticated Building Suit shell read as structural professional application chrome rather than floating decorative cards while preserving all navigation behavior.

USER / PROBLEM: Current desktop chrome uses padded/gapped layout plus rounded/elevated sidebar and top header, and navigation grouping can carry excessive decorative emphasis.

CURRENT-STATE EVIDENCE: Inspect BsAppShell, BsSideMenu, BsTopHeader, Ledger/Shop/Inventory consumers, responsive navigation, account/context slots, focus return, keyboard behavior, RTL and themes.

REFERENCE-PATTERN EVIDENCE: Research one strong enterprise shell/navigation reference plus one relevant operational/admin product. Extract structure, active hierarchy, responsive collapse and context behavior; do not copy branding.

BUILDING SUIT ADAPTATION: Use existing tokens/components. Prefer flat structural chrome, restrained borders/elevation and quieter group hierarchy while preserving logos, routing, mobile behavior, focus, themes and RTL.
verification_plan: Record focused reference-pattern evidence before implementation.
Capture representative before/after rendered shell evidence.
Verify desktop/mobile, EN/AR, LTR/RTL, light/dark and keyboard/focus.
Run shared UI tests, affected consumer checks and git diff --check.
acceptance_criteria: Desktop shell/navigation reads as structural chrome rather than floating cards.
Active navigation hierarchy is clear without excessive Gold, uppercase/tracking or decorative elevation.
Mobile navigation, focus trapping/return, keyboard behavior, RTL and themes remain correct.
Ledger, Shop and Inventory consumers remain compatible.
No brand-token, framework, routing, permission or domain behavior is changed.

tasks.title: Establish Building Suit page archetype composition contracts
tasks.description:
OBJECTIVE: Turn canonical UI PRO archetypes into documented reusable composition contracts and only the minimal shared support actually needed.

USER / PROBLEM: Without explicit composition contracts, generated pages can repeatedly invent card-heavy dashboard/list/form structures despite the shared library.

CURRENT-STATE EVIDENCE: Inspect BsPageHeader, BsContentSection, BsSectionHeader, BsToolbar, BsTabs, BsStateSurface, BsDialog, BsForm, BsDataTable and docs catalogue before adding anything.

REFERENCE-PATTERN EVIDENCE: For each materially changed archetype, research the concrete UX question rather than broad style inspiration.

BUILDING SUIT ADAPTATION: Document application shell, dashboard, worklist, detail, create/edit, settings, reports, onboarding/auth, wizard, modal/drawer and state patterns without forcing identical pages. Reuse shared components first.
verification_plan: Record research question/reference evidence for each materially implemented archetype capability.
Render representative catalogue examples with realistic state variations.
Run shared UI/UX tests, affected app checks, ownership checks and git diff --check.
Verify Arabic/RTL, themes, narrow layouts, long labels and keyboard/focus where relevant.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical guide defines Building Suit archetypes and expected behavior.
Existing components are mapped to archetypes before new abstraction.
Any new shared support is minimal, explicitly exported and demonstrated.
State, responsive, RTL and theme expectations are part of the contracts.
No domain rule moves into shared presentation.

tasks.title: Professionalize metric hierarchy, sections and surface usage
tasks.description:
OBJECTIVE: Create reusable information-surface patterns that replace equal-weight KPI/card walls with deliberate hierarchy while preserving canonical token values.

USER / PROBLEM: Important dashboards can give materially different indicators equal visual weight and overuse containers, producing generic generated-SaaS composition.

CURRENT-STATE EVIDENCE: Inspect BsCard, BsKpiCard, section components, base styles, token usage and representative Ledger/Shop dashboards. Treat canonical token values as locked unless separately approved.

REFERENCE-PATTERN EVIDENCE: Study metric-summary/dashboard hierarchy in one strong enterprise reference plus one domain product. Extract prioritization, grouping, comparison and drill-through behavior.

BUILDING SUIT ADAPTATION: Prefer typography/spacing/proximity/borders before standalone cards. Add/refine a shared metric summary only where reusable. Keep Gold scarce and reserve stronger elevation for temporary surfaces.
verification_plan: Record reference evidence and why each adopted pattern applies.
Capture rendered before/after examples with realistic values, long labels and narrow layouts.
Run shared checks, affected builds/typechecks and git diff --check.
acceptance_criteria: Reusable primary-metric summary supports a small set of genuinely important measures without one floating card per value.
Ordinary sections can compose without decorative card wrappers where grouping does not require them.
Canonical Building Suit color/radius/typography-family/elevation token values remain unchanged by default.
Gold and semantic colors retain intentional meanings.
BsCard/BsKpiCard remain available where meaningful.

tasks.title: Professionalize tables, forms and working density
tasks.description:
OBJECTIVE: Refine the existing PrimeVue-backed table/form system so operational work feels dense, professional and consistent without adding another grid/form engine.

USER / PROBLEM: Data-heavy pages need integrated search/filter/action behavior, predictable density and consistent forms; decorative wrappers or duplicated controls reduce efficiency.

CURRENT-STATE EVIDENCE: Inspect BsDataTable, BsTableDensity, BsToolbar, BsForm, fields/selects/dialogs, shared controllers, lazy-query semantics and Ledger/Shop consumers.

REFERENCE-PATTERN EVIDENCE: Use one best-in-class data-table/index reference and one domain reference; use a mature settings/form pattern where form behavior changes. Extract query, selection, bulk-action, density, dirty-state and error behavior.

BUILDING SUIT ADAPTATION: Keep BsDataTable/BsForm/BsDialog/useRecordAction/useConfirmation authoritative. Improve composition/contracts rather than replacing PrimeVue or moving authorization to UI.
verification_plan: Use realistic datasets, long content, no-match, empty, loading, error and denied states.
Verify selection/bulk action behavior and failure-state selection preservation where relevant.
Verify EN/AR, LTR/RTL, light/dark, compact/comfortable, keyboard/focus and narrow layouts.
Run shared UI/UX tests, affected product checks, ownership enforcement and git diff --check.
acceptance_criteria: Operational tables can be first-class page work surfaces with coherent integrated search/filter/action placement.
Compact/comfortable density remains usable and query/search ownership is not duplicated.
Forms use consistent labels/hints/errors/sections/actions and preserve pending + dirty-state policy.
Lazy queries, permissions and server authorization remain product-owned.
Keyboard/focus, RTL and loading/empty/error/denied/narrow states remain accessible.

tasks.title: Shop dashboard professional reference pilot
tasks.description:
OBJECTIVE: Implement Shop Dashboard as the first complete product pilot of the approved UI PRO methodology and shared patterns.

USER / PROBLEM: Shop Dashboard contains rich operational data but too many blocks/card-like surfaces receive similar visual treatment, reducing hierarchy.

CURRENT-STATE EVIDENCE: Inspect the real dashboard, report permissions, trial/setup states, branch filters, reports, drill-through routes, loading/denied/error states and calculations. Preserve all functional behavior.

REFERENCE-PATTERN EVIDENCE: Research operational-summary hierarchy, location/date filtering, exceptions and source drill-through using one strong general operational dashboard and one relevant POS/shop-domain reference.

BUILDING SUIT ADAPTATION: Apply Building Suit shell/archetypes/metric/table/form patterns. Prioritize a small set of primary metrics, meaningful exceptions/actions and records. Preserve Shop data, permissions, calculations, subscription/setup behavior and bilingual content.
verification_plan: Record references/pattern decisions and Building Suit adaptation.
Capture before/after screenshots using the same realistic fixture where possible.
Exercise filters, drill-through, owner/employee access and state variations.
Run Shop/app/shared checks appropriate to changed paths and git diff --check.
acceptance_criteria: Rendered Shop Dashboard follows the quiet premium operational language and no longer reads as a wall of equivalent cards.
Primary metrics, filters, exceptions, detail sections and source drill-through have deliberate hierarchy.
All report calculations, permissions, routes, setup/trial/subscription behavior and backend semantics remain unchanged.
Before/after evidence covers desktop/mobile, EN/AR, LTR/RTL, light/dark and relevant states.
Pilot produces an explicit visual handback suitable for operator approval before propagation.

tasks.title: Propagate approved UI PRO patterns across remaining Shop workflows
tasks.description:
OBJECTIVE: Apply only operator-approved pilot patterns across remaining authenticated Shop screens, using workflow-specific research where specialized operations differ from ordinary admin pages.
